??? question "Which planned type would hold values whose count can grow or shrink while the program runs?"

    A vector, `Vector<T>`. It is future work; v0.1 has only fixed-size arrays.

    Introduced in [9. Planned types](05-types-planned-for-later.md).

??? question "What happens when a running Vortex program divides an integer by zero?"

    A runtime error. The program stops and reports what went wrong.

    Introduced in [8. Runtime and numerical rules](06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [10. Diagnostics](../specification/diagnostics.md#runtime-error).

??? question "What does the compiler place in generated code just before an operation that might fail, such as dividing by a variable?"

    A runtime check. It may be left out only when the compiler can prove the operation safe.

    Introduced in [8. Runtime and numerical rules](06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [1. Conformance and terminology](../specification/conformance.md#14-static-and-dynamic-rules).

??? question "What do we call the period while the compiler is working on the source, before any executable exists?"

    Compile time. Errors found then are reported before the program can run.

    Introduced in [8. Runtime and numerical rules](06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What do we call the period while the finished executable is running?"

    Run time. Checks that depend on values known only then are made at run time.

    Introduced in [8. Runtime and numerical rules](06-runtime-and-numerical-rules.md). Specification: [12. Glossary](../specification/glossary.md).

??? question "What kind of type is built into the language and named by a keyword, such as `i32` or `bool`?"

    A primitive type. v0.1 has `void`, `bool`, `char`, `i32`, `u32`, `usize`, `f32`, `f64` and `String`.

    Introduced in [4. Variables and types](04-variables-and-types.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#42-primitive-types).

??? question "In the call `add(3, 4)`, what are `3` and `4` called?"

    Arguments. Each one supplies the value for one parameter, and their number and types must match the parameter list.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [5. Expressions](../specification/expressions.md#calls).

??? question "How do you convert `count` to an `f32` in Vortex, and what is this called?"

    With a cast written like a call, `f32(count)`. A value that does not fit the new type is reported as an error rather than silently changed.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [4. Types and values](../specification/types-and-values.md#412-casts-and-conversions).

??? question "Which planned type is meant for multidimensional numerical data, and what replaces it in v0.1?"

    A tensor. In v0.1 you use a fixed-size multidimensional array such as `[f32; 4, 4]`.

    Introduced in [9. Planned types](05-types-planned-for-later.md).

??? question "Which planned type would view part of an array with a length known only at run time, and what do you use in v0.1 instead?"

    A slice, such as `&[f32]`. In v0.1 you use a reference to a fixed-size array, such as `&[f32; 4]`.

    Introduced in [9. Planned types](05-types-planned-for-later.md).

??? question "What check makes sure `values[index]` stays inside the array, and when does it happen?"

    A bounds check. It happens during compilation when the index is already known, and at run time otherwise.

    Introduced in [5. Expressions](08-expressions.md). Specification: [7. Arrays and shapes](../specification/arrays.md#76-indexing).

??? question "What do we call a place in the program that introduces a name, such as `let width = 128;`?"

    A declaration. Top-level declarations are functions and structs; locals are declared by statements inside blocks.

    Introduced in [7. Declarations](10-declarations.md). Specification: [3. Programs and declarations](../specification/declarations.md#31-program-structure).

??? question "What is the planned kind of function that could run on a GPU, and can you declare one in v0.1?"

    A kernel. No; kernel and parallel syntax are future work, so v0.1 rejects them.

    Introduced in [10. Planned kernels and parallelism](07-kernels-and-parallel-execution.md).
